data.text: In this scenario EBITDA falls 30% to $70M, and refinancing at 10% doubles the interest bill to $40M. Free cash flow drops from $50M to zero, so cash stays stuck at $100M. Leverage rises to 5.71x and coverage falls to 1.75x.
Both loan rules fail. Leverage of 5.71x is over the 5.00x cap, and coverage of 1.75x is under the 2.00x floor.
The case to lend is thin but real: Pizza Co. still earns $70M of EBITDA and isn't burning cash. If the earnings drop is temporary, a waiver and tighter terms could carry it through.

Don't lend. Both rules are broken, at 5.71x leverage and 1.75x coverage. Free cash flow is zero, so the $100M of cash never grows, and $400M still comes due in 2028. We would be lending into a default.
The Bull's case depends on a recovery we can't underwrite. With both rules breached and no free cash flow to build toward the 2028 maturity, the committee votes not to lend.
Don't lend. Leverage of 5.71x breaks the 5.00x cap, coverage of 1.75x breaks the 2.00x floor, and with zero free cash flow there is only $100M to meet $400M due in 2028.
